subject: Tenant-scoped retention toggles & zone-mapping: roadmap ask
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara.park@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Tenant-scoped retention toggles & zone-mapping — implementation Qs

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — FinHealth is excited about Redwood's runtime and the promise of predictable inference cost. As we dig into procurement and compliance, a couple of detailed questions came up from our security and legal teams about retention + regional storage that affect whether we sign the SOW in June. Wanted to send these straight to product/engineering so we can make progress: 

1) Tenant-scoped retention toggles: we need the ability to configure retention per-tenant (workspace) with at least three TTL presets (30d, 90d, indefinite) and the ability to set a custom TTL. Can that be exposed in the admin API and UI (with audit trail)?

2) Zone-mapping: we operate in the EU and need data-at-rest to be constrained to a selected region (e.g., eu-west-1). We also need a fallback rule — if the requested zone is unavailable, requests must fail rather than route to another region.

3) Erasure workflows: on-demand erasures must remove KV caches, embeddings, logs, and any short-lived object stores within 24 hours, and we need a verification proof (audit log entry + exportable confirmation).

I've attached a retention_matrix_v1.xlsx with our suggested defaults and a short design note. Can you route to the right person on your side for a scope estimate and timeline? Our procurement deadline is 2028-06-15.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Sara
Security Operations Lead
FinHealth Inc.

Markus / Karthik — looping you in for E2E feasibility + rough effort estimate. FinHealth is asking for three things that cut across product, storage routing, and erasure tooling. Key asks are: per-tenant TTLs exposed via admin API + UI, strict regional zoning with a "fail closed" fallback, and a proofable on-demand erase that touches caches and embeddings.

Sara — thanks for the clear matrix. I'll coordinate scope and propose a minimal viable implementation that we could commit to for the SOW. Two immediate asks for your team: can you confirm whether the 24-hour erasure SLA is a hard requirement for procurement, and whether FinHealth would accept a phased approach where KV cache erasure is immediate and some archive purge steps are scheduled within 24 hours?

Markus / Karthik — can you reply with a short note on feasibility and what team owners (storage-routing, cache, backend-api) we should assign? If this is a >2 sprint effort, call it out so I can set expectations with the customer.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 14:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Tenant-scoped retention toggles & zone-mapping — implementation Qs

Hi Marissa / Markus / Sara — thanks for the details, Sara. High level notes from engineering after a quick review: 

- Per-tenant TTLs: feasible. We can expose a TenantRetention API with UI controls. Backend changes mainly involve adding a tenant-level metadata field and enforcing TTL at write/delete pipelines. Estimated effort: ~2–3 sprints (backend + UI) for the admin flows and audit logs.

- Zone-mapping "fail closed": this is the tricky piece. Our current routing supports region hints and preferred zones, but automatic failure to error response rather than cross-region fallback will require: 
  * enforcement at the gateway/router layer (small change, ~1 week)
  * a region-availability check matrix and per-tenant policy storage (backend work, ~1 sprint)
  * documentation & operator tooling to prevent accidental global fallback in capacity shortages
Estimated additional effort: ~3 weeks to harden + test. If FinHealth needs firm SLAs on "fail closed" we should add an integration test matrix and a small post-deploy verification job.

- On-demand erasure proof: we have APIs that delete primary storage but currently do not sweep ephemeral KV caches or some model-output caches consistently across variants. We'll need to: 
  * add a purge endpoint that fans out to cache nodes and waits for confirmations (engineering: ~2 sprints)
  * create an audit-log export for erasure events (product/infra: ~1 sprint)
  * provide a proof artifact (signed log export) for customers (security/compliance: small design + docs)

Recommendations for a phased delivery to meet 2028-06-15 SOW cadence: 
1) Phase 1 (target for SOW): TenantRetention API (UI), audit logs for TTL changes, region-preference policy storage, and a documented fallback policy that defaults to fail-closed for EU tenants (configurable by account). Scope: 3 sprints.
2) Phase 2 (post-contract, Q3): Fan-out purge endpoint and signed audit export for erasures; add integration test matrix for fail-closed behavior. Scope: 3–4 sprints.

Open questions for FinHealth (Sara): 
- Would FinHealth accept Phase 1 + contractual commitment to Phase 2 within a defined timeline?
- Are there any other stores (third-party logging, external blob stores) you require us to erase as part of the on-demand workflow?

Happy to run a 30-minute technical call next week to align.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Backend
Redwood Inference
